intro: If you need a place to stay near Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital and want a proper room with a kitchen rather than a cramped hotel box, Walton Suites Sukhumvit is the name that keeps surfacing. It is a 4-star serviced suite property on Sukhumvit Soi 49/11, just 220 metres — roughly a 3-minute walk — from the entrance of Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital. Its 52 units run from 50 to 245 sq m with full kitchens, separate living rooms, washing machines, a rooftop saltwater pool, and a free shuttle to BTS Phrom Phong. Opened in 2019 and renovated in 2024. From approx. THB 2,900/night, rated 8.8 from 881 reviews on Booking.com.

body.html: Sukhumvit Soi 49/11 is a quiet side lane that branches off Soi 49, sitting in the Phrom Phong–Thong Lor corridor. Walton Suites is positioned right at the mouth of the soi, directly opposite the entrance to Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital — the walk is around 220 metres, comfortably done in three minutes, no motorcycle taxi or cab required. That proximity makes it a natural first look for families managing a longer hospital stay, carers rotating in and out, or patients undergoing multi-day treatment.

What sets Walton Suites apart from regular hotels in this neighbourhood is room size and the kitchen. The entry point is the Pool Access Suite at around 26 sq m, but the most popular bookings are the Superior One Bedroom (50 sq m) and up — all the way to the Walton Suite Two Bedroom at 110 sq m. Every unit comes with a full-sized refrigerator and freezer, a stovetop, a washing machine, and a separate living area. That setup delivers genuine practicality for families cooking their own meals or stretching a stay over a week, in a way no standard hotel room can match.

"You cross the road and you are at the hospital entrance — and because the room has a proper kitchen we could cook instead of worrying about meals every day. For anyone staying to look after a patient, having both of those things in the same place makes a real difference."

Real guest reviews on Booking.com and Trip.com consistently praise staff who go well beyond the standard front-desk role — several reviews mention the team helping with hospital appointments, interpreting for doctors, and walking guests through the hospital layout. The rooftop saltwater pool draws favourable comments for its views, and the gym is repeatedly described as well-equipped for a property of this size. The on-site VE/LA Coffee Studio handles breakfast and coffee throughout the day, with positive reviews for both.

It is worth being straight about the BTS situation. BTS Phrom Phong is about 987 metres away — a genuine 12-to-15-minute walk, and in Bangkok heat that can feel long, especially with luggage. The hotel's solution is a free shuttle running to BTS Phrom Phong, EmQuartier, and Samitivej Hospital. Most guests find that works well, but check the departure schedule at the front desk because a handful of reviews noted the shuttle runs in one direction only at certain times, leaving you to catch a cab back.

Two recurring cautions from real reviews are worth noting. First, lower-floor rooms can pick up street noise from morning traffic — ask for a higher floor at check-in. Second, while the 2024 renovation refreshed the property, some reviewers have flagged minor maintenance details in a handful of units: worn bathroom sealant and occasional fixture niggles. None of this translates to a major problem, and management responses show the team is active in addressing reports, but it is worth knowing that a few rooms may not be pristine five-star-sharp.

The bottom line: Walton Suites fits two kinds of guest very well. The first is any family or group connected to Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital who needs to walk back and forth without fuss. The second is a longer-stay business traveller or remote worker who wants a real apartment, not a hotel room. For a weekend city-break couple who want to be near the BTS every morning, there are better-located options in the neighbourhood. Rates run from about THB 2,900 to around THB 5,500 per night depending on room type and season — check across platforms before booking.

honestSummary: Walton Suites Sukhumvit is the best-positioned option on Soi 49/11 for anyone who needs a full-kitchen suite within easy walking distance of Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital. Staff quality is a genuine highlight, rooms are properly large, and the kitchen makes longer stays practical. The trade-off is BTS distance and a price premium over standard hotels in the area.
honestChecks: If you need to be walking distance from BTS every morning — BTS Phrom Phong is nearly 1 km away. The free shuttle helps, but it runs on a schedule. If daily Skytrain access matters more than hospital proximity, look at options closer to Sukhumvit Soi 39.

If you are on a tight budget — rates start around THB 2,900 and rise steeply for larger units. If you do not need the kitchen or the extra square metres, The LA49 Hotel or Quartier by Montraj nearby will cost less for a basic room.

If you are a couple looking for a city-break hotel to explore Bangkok from — the soi is quiet and the location leans toward residential. It works brilliantly as a medical or long-stay base, but for daily sightseeing a property closer to the Skytrain will serve you better.

tips.title: Tell the hotel you are here for medical reasons
tips.body: Staff at Walton Suites are experienced with hospital guests — they can help co-ordinate appointments, provide basic interpretation, and point you through the hospital layout. Mention it at check-in or when booking.

tips.title: Check the shuttle schedule before you head out
tips.body: The free shuttle to BTS Phrom Phong and EmQuartier runs on set departures. Ask the front desk for the day's timetable when you check in. For late-night returns, use Grab — it is cheap and reliable from this area.

tips.title: Request a high floor, city-view side
tips.body: Lower rooms near the street can catch early traffic noise. Ask for a higher floor at check-in — you will also get a noticeably better view over the Sukhumvit skyline.

tips.title: Stock up at Tops Market in EmQuartier
tips.body: There is no supermarket inside Soi 49/11 itself. The free shuttle drops you at EmQuartier, where Tops Market in the basement is well-stocked for groceries, snacks and anything you need to cook in your suite.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Walton Suites Sukhumvit

faq.q: How close is Walton Suites Sukhumvit to Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital?
faq.a: The hotel is about 220 metres from the hospital entrance — roughly a 3-minute walk. The property sits on Sukhumvit Soi 49/11, directly opposite the hospital gate, making it one of the closest places to stay for anyone connected to Samitivej Sukhumvit.

faq.q: How far is Walton Suites Sukhumvit from the BTS?
faq.a: BTS Phrom Phong is approximately 987 metres away — about 12 to 15 minutes on foot. The hotel runs a free shuttle to BTS Phrom Phong and EmQuartier; check the departure schedule at the front desk. For late nights, Grab is reliable and inexpensive from this location.

faq.q: What do rooms at Walton Suites cost and what types are available?
faq.a: Rates start from about THB 2,900 per night for a Superior One Bedroom (50 sq m). The range goes up through Corner Suites (60 sq m), Deluxe Two Bedrooms (75 sq m), Walton Suites (110 sq m) and a Pool Villa at 245 sq m. Every unit includes a full kitchen. Prices vary by season and advance booking.

faq.q: Who is Walton Suites Sukhumvit best suited for?
faq.a: It is ideal for two groups: families or carers connected to Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital who need to walk back and forth easily, and business travellers or remote workers on multi-week stays who want apartment-style space with a real kitchen. It is less ideal for short city-break couples who prioritise walkable BTS access over hospital proximity.

faq.q: Is there free parking at Walton Suites Sukhumvit?
faq.a: Yes — free private parking is available for guests. This is a useful advantage for families driving in from other provinces to attend hospital appointments.
